name: Zoho
summary: Zoho is known for hiring on skills rather than credentials: its careers page says it thinks 'beyond the system of credentialism', and Zoho Schools of Learning offers high school graduates a two-year training programme that includes an internship at Zoho. Candidates commonly report that developer hiring leans heavily on hands-on programming, with a written test followed by coding rounds and technical and HR interviews.
rounds: Written or online test of aptitude and programming (for campus and off-campus drives)
Hands-on programming round, solving problems on a computer
A longer programming task: build a small working application in a few hours (for many developer roles)
Technical interview on your code, projects and fundamentals
looks_for: Programming skill shown in working code, whatever your degree or grades

questions.text: Tell me about something you taught yourself without a course or a teacher. How did you go about it?
covers: What you learned and why
How you learned it: what you read, built and got stuck on
Something you made with it

questions.text: Tell me about a time you stuck with a hard problem for a long time before you solved it.
covers: Why it was hard and what you tried first
How you kept going and when you asked for help
The solution and what it taught you

questions.text: Describe a time you helped a user or customer who was struggling with something you built or supported.
covers: Their problem in their words
How you understood it and fixed it or worked around it
What you changed in the product or your work afterwards

questions.text: Tell me about a bug in your code that someone else found. What did you do?
covers: What the bug was, owned plainly
How you fixed it and thanked the person who found it
What you now do to catch such bugs yourself

questions.text: How would you build a simple invoicing app for small businesses? What would you build first, and how would you store the data?
covers: Core entities: customer, item, invoice, payment, and how they relate
The first version: create, send and record payment, before reports and extras
Details that matter: tax such as GST, invoice numbering, rounding

questions.text: Explain object-oriented programming using an example you would build, such as a bank account or library system.
covers: Classes and objects, encapsulation, inheritance and polymorphism, shown in the example
Why each helps in that example
When you'd avoid inheritance and use composition instead

questions.text: You have a few hours to build a small console application, such as appointment booking for a clinic. How would you plan your time?
covers: Listing the features and deciding the order to build them
Choosing classes and data structures before coding
Getting the main flow working first, then edge cases such as full slots and cancellations

questions.text: How does a web app keep a user logged in? Explain sessions, cookies and tokens.
covers: Session IDs stored on the server versus signed tokens the client holds
Where cookies fit, and settings that protect them
Logging out, expiry, and what happens if a token is stolen

questions.text: How would you design search for a business email product so it's fast and keeps each customer's data separate?
covers: An index per mailbox or per customer, updated as mail arrives
Access checks on every query so no one sees another customer's mail
Ranking, speed for large mailboxes, and encryption

questions.text: A customer says a report in your product shows the wrong totals. How would you handle it?
covers: Acknowledging it quickly and reproducing it with their data
Likely causes: time zones, rounding, filters, duplicate records
The fix, an update to the customer, and a test that would catch it again

questions.text: Explain database normalisation. When might you choose to denormalise?
covers: Removing duplicated data so each fact lives in one place
The normal forms in plain words, with an example table
Denormalising for read speed, and the cost of keeping copies in sync

questions.text: Why Zoho? What do you know about the products it builds and the customers who use them?
covers: A few Zoho products and the kind of businesses that use them
What draws you to building software products
Something about how Zoho says it works that suits you

questions.text: Are you open to relocating to wherever the team you join is based, even if it's a smaller town?
covers: An honest answer, with any limits stated clearly
What you'd value about working there
How you'd settle in and keep learning

questions.text: Where do you want your skills to be in five years?
covers: A realistic picture of the work you want to be doing
The skills you plan to build to get there
How a long stay at a product company fits that plan

tips: Zoho's careers page says it looks beyond credentials; let your code and projects do the talking, whatever your degree or college.
Practise writing complete, working programs from scratch in one language you know well; the programming rounds reward fluent basics.
In a longer build task, get the core flow working first and add features one at a time; a working small app beats a half-finished big one.
Learn what a few Zoho products do (for example CRM, Books, Desk and Mail) so you can connect your answers to real customers.
If you're finishing school, Zoho Schools of Learning is a separate route from graduate hiring; check its official page for current eligibility.
